Doc.Summary: Gives the nodes the type. A corner only changes the type, the handles stay. A smooth or symmetric node first needs its handles on one line on opposite sides: if it has an out handle, the direction of that handle wins and the in handle turns to the opposite side (with its own length for smooth, with the length of the out handle for symmetric), and if it only has an in handle the out handle follows it in the same way. A node without handles gets handles on the line from its previous to its next neighbor, a third of the distance to the neighbor on each side (for symmetric both as long as the shorter one). An end node of an open path only gets the handle toward its one neighbor. No handle is created toward a neighbor on the same spot.

Exceptions.Description: An index is not the index of a node, or the type is not defined.

Doc.Summary: Makes a segment straight: the handles that belong to it are removed. A node that lost a handle becomes a corner. A segment that is already straight leaves the path as it is.

Doc.Summary: The path with every sub-path running the other way. An open sub-path gets its node order reversed. A closed sub-path keeps its first node first and the other nodes run backwards, so the start point does not move. In both cases the in and out handle of every node are swapped. Each sub-path stays at its place in the list. The shape is the same, every node stays at the same place on the screen (also for a rotated path), and id, appearance, name, flags, rotation and fill rule are kept. Reversing twice gives the same nodes. The input is not changed.

Whether the point (before any rotation) hits the path. The inside counts for the closed sub-paths, and for all sub-paths if the path has a fill (an open sub-path with a fill is filled as if it were closed). The sub-paths are counted together with the fill rule, so a sub-path inside another one is a hole. An open sub-path, or any sub-path of a path with a stroke, is also hit near its outline: within half the stroke width, but at least a few document units. The closing line of an open sub-path is not part of the outline.

Params.BottomLeft: Radius of the bottom left corner.

Doc.Summary: A point of a path in document units, in the frame of the path before its rotation. Used to build and edit a PressToShape.Core.Shapes.PathShape, which stores its nodes as fractions of its box (PressToShape.Core.Shapes.PathNode).

One run of connected nodes in document units, in the frame of the path before its rotation. Used to build and edit a PressToShape.Core.Shapes.PathShape, which stores its sub-paths as fractions of its box (PressToShape.Core.Shapes.SubPath). Immutable by convention: the list is not changed.
An axis-aligned ellipse that fills its bounds.
How the inside of a path is decided where it crosses itself.

A group of shapes that is selected, moved and styled as one. Children keep their own document coordinates, so a group has no transform. Its box is the union of the rotated bounds of its children, always upright (PressToShape.Core.Shapes.Shape.Rotation is 0), and follows PressToShape.Core.Shapes.GroupShape.Children by itself. Do not set the box, the rotation or the appearance of a group: change its children. Immutable: change it with with.
Measures and wraps a text. The model has no text engine, so the app implements this with its own and tests use a fake. Point text is not wrapped. Area text wraps at the width of its box.
Turns a text into the closed contours of its glyphs. The app implements this with its font engine, tests use a fake.
One laid-out line of a text.

Params.Text: The characters of the line, without the line break.
Params.X: Start of the line, relative to the left edge of the text's box, in document units. It follows the alignment.
Params.Baseline: Baseline of the line, relative to the top edge of the text's box, in document units.

Doc.Summary: Which of the two handles of a node: the one toward the previous node or the one toward the next node.

How the two handles of a node relate when one of them is edited. The type is a rule for editing: a model value that does not match its type (for example after a non-uniform resize) is not an error, the next handle edit enforces the type again.

The rules that connect a PressToShape.Core.Shapes.NodeType with the handles of a node. A node counts as having its handles on one line when the sine of the angle between them is below 1e-6, and as equally long when the lengths differ by less than 1e-6 of the longer one.
The checks shared by PressToShape.Core.Shapes.PathNode and PressToShape.Core.Shapes.DocumentNode, so both refuse the same values.

The nodes of a PressToShape.Core.Shapes.PathShape in document coordinates as lists that an edit can change, one list per sub-path. A node is addressed by its flat index (see PressToShape.Core.Shapes.PathShape.Locate). PressToShape.Core.Shapes.PathBuffer.Build makes the edited path.

Operations that change the nodes of a PressToShape.Core.Shapes.PathShape: add a point, delete a point, continue an open sub-path. Nodes and segments are addressed by their flat index across the sub-paths. Every result is a new path, the input is never changed.

A point of a PressToShape.Core.Shapes.PathShape as it is stored: the anchor and the optional handle points are fractions of the path's box, so 0 is the left or top edge and 1 the right or bottom edge. Handle points may lie outside 0..1. Resizing the box scales the path without touching the nodes. A segment is a curve if the node it starts at has an out handle or the node it ends at has an in handle, otherwise it is a line.

The rules for editing the nodes and handles of a PressToShape.Core.Shapes.PathShape. A node is addressed by its flat index across the sub-paths (see PressToShape.Core.Shapes.PathShape.Locate) and an edit changes only the sub-path that holds it. Every method takes the path and positions in the frame of the path before its rotation (see PressToShape.Core.Shapes.PathShape.ToLocal), changes nothing in place and returns a new path built with PressToShape.Core.Shapes.PathShape.Rebuilt, so every node that was not moved keeps its place on the screen, also for a rotated path.
Reverses the direction of a PressToShape.Core.Shapes.PathShape without changing how it looks.

A path of line and cubic bezier segments made of one or more sub-paths, each open or closed. The box (PressToShape.Core.Shapes.Shape.X, PressToShape.Core.Shapes.Shape.Y, PressToShape.Core.Shapes.Shape.Width, PressToShape.Core.Shapes.Shape.Height) is the tight bounds of all the curves, and the nodes are stored as fractions of that box (see PressToShape.Core.Shapes.PathNode), so changing the box with with moves, resizes and (with the rotation) turns the whole path, like any other shape. Build one from document coordinates with PressToShape.Core.Shapes.PathShape.Create. A node or a segment is addressed by one flat index that counts across the sub-paths, the first sub-path first (see PressToShape.Core.Shapes.PathShape.Locate). Immutable: change it with with.
An axis-aligned rectangle, with square or rounded corners.

One corner of a rounded rectangle: its radius, the corner point of the box, and where the arc starts and ends when the outline is followed clockwise. For a radius of 0 the arc is empty and PressToShape.Core.Shapes.RoundedCorner.Start and PressToShape.Core.Shapes.RoundedCorner.End are the corner point.

Params.Point: The corner point of the box.
Params.Start: Where the arc starts, coming along the previous edge.
Params.End: Where the arc ends, going on along the next edge.

Doc.Summary: The outline of a rectangle with rounded corners, in the frame before any rotation. The conversion to a path and the SVG export both start from these points, so the two outlines are the same shape.
A drawable shape with a position, a size and an appearance. Immutable: change it with with. Values are validated on creation and on with.
Turns shapes into paths without changing how they look, so they can be edited node by node.

One run of connected nodes of a PressToShape.Core.Shapes.PathShape, open or closed. The nodes are stored the way the path stores them, as fractions of the box of the whole path (see PressToShape.Core.Shapes.PathNode). Immutable.
How the lines of a text are aligned. For point text the lines align to each other, for area text to the box.
A change of the formatting of texts. Each value that is set replaces the one of the text, a value that is null leaves it as it is.

Params.FontFamily: The font family name, or null.
Params.IsBold: Bold on or off, or null.
Params.IsItalic: Italic on or off, or null.
Params.LineSpacing: The line spacing multiplier, or null.

Doc.Summary: The result of laying out a text.

Params.Lines: The lines from top to bottom. Empty for an empty text.
Params.Width: Width of the widest line in document units.
Params.Height: Height of all lines together in document units.

Doc.Summary: A text with one font setting for the whole object. Point text (PressToShape.Core.Shapes.TextShape.IsArea false) grows with its content and its box is the measured extent, which the app writes after each measure. Area text wraps at the width of its box. The model does not measure or wrap, see ITextMeasurer.
